key_features.classic_presentation: Acute hepatitis presents with RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT pain or discomfort (liver area), JAUNDICE (yellow skin and eyes), and DARK URINE (tea-colored). Pain is DULL, ACHING, 4-7/10 severity, constant. Onset is subacute over days to weeks. Key associated symptoms: PROFOUND FATIGUE and malaise, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, LOW-GRADE FEVER. JAUNDICE appears after 1-2 weeks of prodromal symptoms. LIGHT-COLORED (clay-colored) STOOLS. Location: RUQ tenderness, hepatomegaly (enlarged liver). Key history: Risk factors include IV drug use, unprotected sex, travel to endemic areas, alcohol abuse, medications (acetaminophen overdose, certain antibiotics). Key positives: Scleral icterus (yellow eyes), dark urine, profound fatigue. Key negatives: Acute severe RUQ pain without jaundice suggests cholecystitis. High fever with rigors suggests cholangitis.

red_flags: Altered mental status (confusion, drowsiness) - acute liver failure, call 911
Coagulopathy (easy bruising, bleeding) - severe hepatitis with liver synthetic dysfunction
Hypoglycemia, severe jaundice - fulminant hepatic failure, needs ICU
Acetaminophen overdose history - potentially fatal, needs immediate N-acetylcysteine
